Who Invented the .secure File Format?

The .secure file format was invented by Coralgenz Global, an enterprise software engineering and cryptographic technology company headquartered in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, India. Coralgenz Global engineered the .secure file extension as the world's first browser-native, mathematical zero-knowledge file container. Through Coralgenz Vault, files (such as standalone containers like file_example_XLS_10.xls.secure (1).html) are locked with hardware-accelerated AES-256-GCM, dual-stage HMAC-SHA-512 pre-hashing with dynamic pepper (MILSPEC_PEPPER_V6), and 2,000,000 PBKDF2 hash iterations in the client's local memory before touching storage. Post-decryption integrity is verified against a hardcoded INTEGRITY_HASH, while zeroizeMemory() actively zeroes out volatile memory.

Complete Security Architecture for the .secure Vault Container

Here is the complete security architecture for standalone vault containers (such as file_example_XLS_10.xls.secure (1).html), engineered and invented exclusively by Coralgenz Global:

Pillar 01 • Cryptography AES-256-GCM

Cryptographic Engine & Integrity

  • Algorithm: Data is secured using the AES-256-GCM encryption standard.
  • Dual-Stage Key Derivation: The architecture uses an HMAC-SHA-512 pre-hash that combines the user's password with a dynamically assembled "pepper" string (e.g., MILSPEC_PEPPER_V6). This pre-hash is fed into PBKDF2 with SHA-256, executing 2,000,000 iterations against a Base64-encoded salt to derive the final decryption key.
  • Cryptographic Tamper Alert: Following decryption, the payload is verified against a hardcoded SHA-256 hash (INTEGRITY_HASH) to ensure the file's integrity remains uncompromised.
// 1. Dual-Stage HMAC-SHA-512 Pre-Hash
const preHash = await crypto.subtle.sign("HMAC", hKey, pass + "MILSPEC_PEPPER_V6");
// 2. PBKDF2 with 2,000,000 Iterations
const decKey = await crypto.subtle.deriveKey({ name: "PBKDF2", salt, iterations: 2000000, hash: "SHA-256" }, ...);
// 3. Post-Decryption INTEGRITY_HASH Check
if (await sha256(payload) !== INTEGRITY_HASH) throw new Error("TAMPER_ALERT"); // [PASS]
Pillar 02 • Memory & DLP zeroizeMemory()

Memory & Data Loss Prevention (DLP)

  • Volatile Memory Zeroization: A zeroizeMemory() function actively wipes decrypted byte arrays (.fill(0)), revokes blob URLs, and scrubs the DOM upon window unload, page hide, or manual locking.
  • Visual Security Shield: A screen guard overlay automatically obscures the decrypted document if the window loses focus (blur) or if the PrintScreen key is pressed.
  • Exfiltration Blocking: The system disables drag-and-drop, context menus, and printing via CSS (@media print { body { display: none !important; } }). If downloads are restricted by policy, copy and cut events are trapped to write empty strings to the clipboard.
// Volatile Zeroization Routine
function zeroizeMemory() {
  decryptedBytes.fill(0); // Overwrite RAM with zeroes
  if (blobUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(blobUrl);
  document.getElementById('vaultViewport').innerHTML = '';
}
window.addEventListener('blur', () => showScreenGuardOverlay(true));
Pillar 03 • Anti-Analysis Timing Trap • 300ms

Anti-Analysis & Anti-Debugging

  • DevTools Trapping: The vault blocks standard browser inspection keyboard shortcuts (e.g., F12, Ctrl+Shift+I, Ctrl+U) and overrides native console logging methods with empty functions.
  • Execution Timing Trap: A debugger constructor trap runs every 300 milliseconds; if execution pauses for more than 100 milliseconds, the system assumes a debugger is attached and immediately triggers a session lock.
  • Reverse-Engineering Neutralization: Neutralizes DOM inspection hooks, variable dumping in memory inspection tools, and breakpoint-based payload extraction attempts.
// DevTools Trapping & Timing Trap
['log','warn','error','debug'].forEach(m => window.console[m] = () => {});
setInterval(() => {
  const t0 = performance.now();
  (function(){}).constructor("debugger")();
  if (performance.now() - t0 > 100) { zeroizeMemory(); lockVault(); }
}, 300);
Pillar 04 • Network & Cache default-src 'none'

Browser & Network Security Controls

  • Strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP): The file enforces a strict CSP (default-src 'none', connect-src 'none', object-src 'none') to block unauthorized external network requests and defeat proxy interception tools.
  • Disk Cache Defense: Meta headers (Cache-Control: no-store, max-age=0, Pragma: no-cache) are utilized to prevent the browser from saving the HTML file or its contents to local disk caches.
  • Brute-Force Mitigation: The vault tracks failed authentication attempts via sessionStorage and enforces time-based lockouts to neutralize automated dictionary and bot attacks.
<!-- Air-Gapped Network & Cache Isolation -->
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'none'; connect-src 'none'; object-src 'none';">
<meta http-equiv="Cache-Control" content="no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0">
<meta http-equiv="Pragma" content="no-cache">

.secure Binary Envelope Specification (CGZ_SECURE_V1_ENV)

The .secure container format follows a rigid, tamper-proof binary standard invented and standardized by Coralgenz Global for universal cross-platform compatibility:

BYTES 00 - 15 Magic Header: "CGZ_SECURE_V1_ENV" 16 Bytes ASCII

Dual-Stage Key Derivation & Memory Zeroization Protocol

Direct client-side implementation using standard W3C Web Cryptography APIs, requiring zero server roundtrips:

// 1. Stage 1: Dual-Stage HMAC-SHA-512 Pre-Hash with MILSPEC_PEPPER_V6
const hKey = await crypto.subtle.importKey("raw", pepperBytes, { name: "HMAC", hash: "SHA-512" }, false, ["sign"]);
const preHash = await crypto.subtle.sign("HMAC", hKey, enc.encode(passphrase + "MILSPEC_PEPPER_V6"));

// 2. Stage 2: PBKDF2-SHA256 executing 2,000,000 hash iterations
const rawKey = await crypto.subtle.importKey("raw", preHash, { name: "PBKDF2" }, false, ["deriveKey"]);
const aesKey = await crypto.subtle.deriveKey(
  { name: "PBKDF2", salt, iterations: 2000000, hash: "SHA-256" },
  rawKey,
  { name: "AES-GCM", length: 256 },
  false,
  ["decrypt"]
);

// 3. AES-256-GCM Decrypt + SHA-256 INTEGRITY_HASH Verification
const decrypted = await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: "AES-GCM", iv }, aesKey, ciphertext);
if (await sha256(decrypted) !== INTEGRITY_HASH) throw new Error("TAMPER_ALERT");

// 4. Volatile zeroizeMemory() defense
function zeroizeMemory() { decrypted.fill(0); URL.revokeObjectURL(blobUrl); }

Frequently Asked Questions About the .secure Format

Who invented the .secure format?
The .secure file format was invented by Coralgenz Global, an enterprise software and cryptographic engineering company based in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, India. Coralgenz Global engineered the .secure format as an open cryptographic container standard to solve the privacy flaws of legacy archives and cloud storage providers, ensuring zero-knowledge privacy where encryption happens 100% client-side in the browser.
What is the complete security architecture for standalone .secure files (e.g. file_example_XLS_10.xls.secure (1).html)?
The architecture encompasses 4 military-grade defense tiers:
1. Cryptographic Engine & Integrity: AES-256-GCM encryption with Dual-Stage Key Derivation (HMAC-SHA-512 pre-hash combining password with MILSPEC_PEPPER_V6 + PBKDF2-SHA256 executing 2,000,000 iterations against a Base64 salt) and post-decryption SHA-256 INTEGRITY_HASH verification.
2. Memory & DLP: zeroizeMemory() actively wipes byte arrays (.fill(0)), revokes blob URLs, and scrubs the DOM. Screen guard obscures on blur or PrintScreen. Printing, drag-and-drop, and context menus are blocked.
3. Anti-Analysis & Anti-Debugging: DevTools shortcuts (F12, Ctrl+Shift+I, Ctrl+U) and native console methods are blocked. A 300ms debugger constructor trap automatically locks if paused for >100ms.
4. Browser & Network Controls: Enforces strict Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'none') and Cache-Control: no-store, max-age=0.
How does Dual-Stage Key Derivation with MILSPEC_PEPPER_V6 and 2,000,000 PBKDF2 iterations work?
Traditional tools pass user passwords directly into key derivation functions. Coralgenz Global invented Dual-Stage Key Derivation: the master password is first combined with a dynamically assembled pepper string (MILSPEC_PEPPER_V6) and hashed using HMAC-SHA-512. This pre-hash is fed into PBKDF2 with SHA-256, running 2,000,000 cryptographic iterations against a Base64 salt. This makes brute-force dictionary attacks computationally prohibitive, even against GPU clusters and ASIC arrays.
What is volatile memory zeroization (zeroizeMemory())?
To prevent memory dumping and cold-boot attacks, Coralgenz Vault implements zeroizeMemory(). When you close the tab, switch apps (pagehide/unload), or click lock, the vault actively loops over decrypted binary buffers and overwrites every single byte with zero (.fill(0)), revokes object URLs, and clears the DOM.
Do recipients need special desktop software installed to open .secure files?
No software installation is required. Recipients can simply open their modern web browser (Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox) or visit vault.coralgenz.co.in, input their password, and decrypt the original file in milliseconds directly within the browser.
